In August 1998, two grad students got a one-hundred-thousand-dollar check for a simple idea. Today, that idea is worth about three and a half trillion dollars. And it's number one on this list. We picked ten famous simple ideas, and ranked them by what they're worth today, as of November sixteenth, 2026. Let's count down.
narr
Number ten. A ride, at the tap of a button. In 2009, Garrett Camp had the idea that became UberCab. It dropped the 'Cab' in 2011. Today, Uber is worth about one hundred forty-three billion dollars.
narr

Number nine. A kitchen that worked like an assembly line. In 1948, the McDonald brothers created their Speedee Service System in San Bernardino, California. In 1955, Ray Kroc joined the story. Today, McDonald's is worth about one hundred ninety-four billion.
narr
Number eight. Movies, by mail. Netflix was founded in August 1997 as a DVD rental service. The envelopes are gone, but the idea grew up. Today, Netflix is worth about two hundred forty-nine billion.
narr
Number seven. A drink, for five cents a glass. On May 8th, 1886, Coca-Cola was first sold at Jacob's Pharmacy in Atlanta. Today, the company is worth about four hundred twenty-eight billion dollars.
narr
Number six. A warehouse you pay to shop in. Costco opened its first warehouse in Seattle in September 1983. Today, it's worth about four hundred ninety-four billion.
narr

Number five. A card that lets you pay later. In September 1958, Bank of America launched the BankAmericard in Fresno, California. That card program grew into Visa. Today, Visa is worth about seven hundred ninety-six billion dollars.
narr
Number four. Low prices, in a small town. On July 2nd, 1962, the first Wal-Mart Discount City opened in Rogers, Arkansas. Today, Walmart is worth about one trillion dollars.
